source_records.title: Consumption tax and corporate product mix decisions
source_records.abstract: This paper examines how consumption taxes—through the taxation of input goods—can affect firms' product mix decisions. We study India's staggered transition from a sales tax, where there was the risk that intermediate inputs are taxed multiple times along the supply chain, to a value-added tax (VAT) that offered credits for taxes paid on inputs. Using detailed product-level data for manufacturing firms and a stacked difference-in-differences design, we find that firms respond to the VAT adoption by narrowing their product scope through reducing vertical integration. These changes reflect a shift away from internal production of inputs, which was tax-induced under the sales tax system, toward greater specialization in the most profitable outputs. We also document that this vertical disintegration leads to lower manufacturing costs, greater profitability, improved investment efficiency, and higher firm value. Our findings highlight how consumption tax design can affect resource allocation within firms and that reducing tax burdens on input goods enhances operational efficiency.

source_records.title: Consumption tax and corporate product mix decisions
source_records.abstract: This paper examines how consumption taxes—through the taxation of input goods—can affect firms' product mix decisions. We study India's staggered transition from a sales tax, where there was the risk that intermediate inputs are taxed multiple times along the supply chain, to a value-added tax (VAT) that offered credits for taxes paid on inputs. Using detailed product-level data for manufacturing firms and a stacked difference-in-differences design, we find that firms respond to the VAT adoption by narrowing their product scope through reducing vertical integration. These changes reflect a shift away from internal production of inputs, which was tax-induced under the sales tax system, toward greater specialization in the most profitable outputs. We also document that this vertical disintegration leads to lower manufacturing costs, greater profitability, improved investment efficiency, and higher firm value. Our findings highlight how consumption tax design can affect resource allocation within firms and that reducing tax burdens on input goods enhances operational efficiency.

before.title_zh: 消费税与企业产品组合决策
before.abstract_zh: 本文考察消费税——通过对投入品征税——如何影响企业的产品组合决策。我们研究印度从销售税到增值税（VAT）的分阶段过渡，在销售税下，中间投入品存在沿供应链被多次征税的风险，而增值税则对投入品已纳税款提供抵扣。利用制造业企业详细的产品层面数据以及堆叠双重差分设计，我们发现企业通过减少垂直整合来收窄其产品范围，以回应增值税的采用。这些变化反映了从内部生产投入品——在销售税制度下这是税收引致的——转向在最具盈利性的产出上实现更大程度的专业化。我们还记录到，这种垂直分离带来了更低的制造成本、更高的盈利能力、改善的投资效率以及更高的企业价值。我们的发现凸显了消费税设计如何影响企业内部的资源配置，并且降低投入品的税收负担能够提升运营效率。
